reason: Factually wrong on its central measurement, and its fix would break the gate it claims to keep clean. (1) THE BREAKPOINT IS 701, NOT 767. Driven in chromium at 390/420/480/560/640/690/700/701/720/767/768/900 on owner-flight, .b-num/.b-when/.b-title/.b-away step 96->148, 20->30, 17->24, 15->17 at exactly 701px (b.css:1209 '@media (min-width: 701px)', announced in the file header: 'Every value here is the phone value and the desk values live inside @media (min-width: 701px)'). At 701-766 all four are ALREADY at desk values, so 'identical from 390 to 766' and 'every one of them jumps at 767' are both false. The finding sampled 700 and 767 and inferred a threshold it never located. The real frozen stretch is 391-700 (310px), not 376px, and 700 is the single pixel below the boundary - every breakpoint system in existence has that property one pixel below its threshold, so 'at 700px it is still the phone size' is not evidence of anything. The column at 700 is 620px, not 660px. (2) THE RAMP CLAIM IS FALSE. 'The declared typeRamp carries 20, 24, 30 and 48 steps that this band never uses' - 20 IS .b-when's phone size, 24 IS .b-title's desk size, 30 IS .b-when's desk size. All three are in active use on one side or the other of 701. (3) THE FIX FAILS THE MEASURED GATE. The proposal asserts 'All four values are already on ladders.typeRamp'. ladders.typeRamp is [11,12,13,15,17,20,24,30,38,48,64,96,148]. 120 is not on it and no --size-* token carries it. Shipping .b-num at 120px would trip audit.mjs's ramp check - the exact opposite of what the finding promises. It also inverts the semantic tokens: it puts --size-head ('a moment title at desk width') on the date line and --size-date ('the ceremonial date line') on a moment title. (4) 701 IS NOT A TYPE BREAKPOINT, IT IS THE GEOMETRY SWITCH. The same query moves the rail 90->100, the item/origin/measure lane 110->124, the .b-away box -110/76 -> -124/84, three tick offsets, and turns .b-bar into flex. Type changes there because the instrument it sits on changes there - one coordinated phone->desk switch, which is why 'one breakpoint doing all the work for four objects' is the point, not the flaw. A type-only step at 560 would put desk-scale type on phone-scale rail geometry (24px titles and a 120px numeral against a 480px field, a 330px copy box, and an unwidened 76px away lane) and add a second, weaker switching point the layout does not otherwise honour. That is strictly worse. (5) IT DOES NOT TOUCH THE AUDIENCE SURFACE. phone, day, ended and loading are data-medium='phone' and pinned to a 390px stage at any viewport - measured at 700px: stage 390, num 96, title 17 for all of them. The guest's screen is 390px wide whatever the window is, so a 560px breakpoint would change nothing for the person this artifact is actually for. It would only affect owner-facing states. (6) AT A 9.5 BAR, ONE PHONE RAMP TO ~700 IS THE DECISION, NOT THE DEFECT. Linear, Stripe and Vercel all hold a single mobile type scale across the whole sub-768 range; the lab's own viewport list is 390 and 768, both correctly on their own side of 701. This is taste stated as a defect, resting on a measurement that is wrong by 66 pixels.
